page.layout: Running head above the text, printed page number at top left. One column of running text, continuing from the previous page, with an italic dating note set below it at full width. Then a title block, a speaker's name and a verse poem in italic, all at full width. No marginal notes. The right edge of the scan shows the neighbouring page and is left out.

main_text.p: meritò: Agnoscimus, ô Deus, accusamus, damnamus nos & peccata nostra, quibus tu pestilente gladiū superiore anno visum fuerat immittere, tum hoc succedente anno lumē illud præstantissimum, quod in illustri celebris huius scholæ candelabro statueras (prout minatus eras iadiu) extinguere. Oramus te, ô Deus & pater miserationum, ne porro sœvias in hunc pusillum gregem nostrum, neque rationem nobiscum ineas, aut cum peccatis nostris, ut ira tua amplius exardescente de via iusta pereamus.

Sed potius quandoquidem vexillū filii tu hic constitui gratiosissimè voluisti, fideq. dedisti beatos fore qui sese ad te receperint: rege nos, ô Deus, tuo spiritu, ut osculemur filii dilectionis tuæ, & salute omne[?] ab eo expectemus: Satanæ consilia & conatus perde: populum tuum coferua, ecclesiæ huic, scholæ, & regioni toti bonos fidelesque pastores, doctores & administros confer:tuere quos dedisti, & auge omni benedictionum genere, populares atq. studiosos in officio iusto, sanctimonia, charitate, & pace continue, omnia denique in nobis perfice, ut Deus omnipotens & pater optimus noster, quæ ad gloriam tui nominis, communem ædificationem, & salutem nostram pertinebunt in Christo Iesu Domino nostro, qui tecum vivit regnatque in unitate spiritus, æternus Deus in secula, Amen.

p.i: Neapoli Nemetum obdormiuit in Christo placidis-sime die 6. Mart. hora vesper. 6. anno 1583. cum vixisset annos 48 menf. 6. horas 11. sepultus 8. Mart. in templi choro.

main_text.head: EXEQUIIS D. ZACHARIÆ URSINI, PRÆCEPTORIS SUI COLENDISSIMI,

p.i: OURSINE sacros inter celeberrime Vates, Quos modo sincerus numinis ardor agit, Siccin' abit? ô & iuuenum[?] ter maxime cultor, Quo fugis? ô nostra lux que decusque schola: Cur nos tam dubio rerum sub turbine linquis, Ceu rate si mediis nauita cedat aquis[?]

page.notes: Running head and dating note are set in italic; the dating note is one block under the main text. Several readings are doubtful: "quod" in line 2 of the first paragraph ("quoð"), "iadiu", "salute omne" (print unclear), "tuuenum" in the verse, and the last word of the verse, which may be "aquis" or "aquu". The verse initial O is a large initial joined to "URSINE". Heading level 1 is used for the title of the poem. Signature "Te," is read from the bottom right corner with uncertainty.
